environment.description: Identical Node.js 20 Apollo Server 4.x deployment on ECS Fargate behind ALB. Session credentials use a rotating HMAC-based token scheme where the signing key is derived from a Secrets Manager secret that undergoes automatic rotation via a Lambda rotator on a 60-second schedule (AWS::SecretsManager::RotationSchedule with RotationRules.AutomaticallyAfterDays replaced by custom cron rate(1 minute)). The session token includes a timestamp-bucketed HMAC component; upon key rotation the previous key is retained for a 5-second grace window only. The ALB sticky session is disabled. Additionally, the ECS task role has an IAM permission boundary that denies secretsmanager:GetSecretValue except from the application's own task, preventing lateral read of the current signing key. The Redis session store TTL is set to 55 seconds (below rotation interval), meaning any session cookie presented by a CSRF attack page would reference an expired or invalid HMAC by the time the victim's browser executes the forged request (typical CSRF attack setup time exceeds 60s for social engineering delivery).

config.secret_rotation: AWS Secrets Manager, custom Lambda rotator, rate(1 minute)
config.iam_permission_boundary: deny secretsmanager:GetSecretValue except task role ARN
